method: Each episode row is post-action. grid_hash equality means equal rendered grid; it does not prove equal hidden state. explorer_actions counts non-null explorer_branch, including top_branch induce.no_plan.explorer. Early stop without level-up/error is inferred as explored_out from policy code, not logged.

ar25.registry_action_model: Keyboard-only ACTION1-4 movement plus ACTION5 selection cycling (cycles horizontal mirror, then vertical mirror, then each disconnected movable sprite separately). L3 tail: ACTION1 x7 moves the selected horizontal axis up, ACTION5 selects the L-shaped object, ACTION4 x7 and ACTION2 x7 place it, ACTION5 selects the two-row object, then ACTION3 x12 and ACTION2 x5 place it. L4-L8: decompose each disconnected glyph into its component sprites and place each into its matching target orbit; L5 has a one-column anchor gotcha (large sprite starts at logical column 14, not 15 -- move left 10, not 11). Full 253-action winning sequence in results/outer_loop_codex_ar25_probe.json. ACTION6/ACTION7 are non-load-bearing (ACTION7 pops a hidden undo stack, deliberately excluded).

cn04.registry_action_model: ACTION1-4 move the selected visible sprite; ACTION5 rotates a singleton selected sprite or cycles a stacked variant; ACTION6 selects a visible sprite through camera-derived display coordinates. L4+: ACTION5 semantics are PER-SPRITE and PER-LEVEL -- rigid 90-degree rotation on L4, but shape-VARIANT cycling starting at L5 (see gotcha below).

g50t.registry_action_model: Keyboard ACTION1 up, ACTION2 down, ACTION3 left, ACTION4 right, ACTION5 commit/rewind clone. L2 uses two clone cycles: first clone holds the right-hand plate, second clone holds the left-hand plate, then the active player takes the top route to the target-offset cell.

ka59.registry_action_model: mixed keyboard+click [4,4,4,3,2,3,3,3,C:1,1,4]; C:1 dynamically clicks the second movable block after the first block is placed. L2-L4 extends this with plain ACTION1-5 move/select labels and explicit "6:x:y" ACTION6 coordinate-click labels (frame pixel coords) for selecting e-framed blocks -- see experiment_4460_submission_package_prep.py:resolve_replay_plan's ka59 branch for the exact apply-function extension needed to replay these.

ls20.registry_action_model: Keyboard ACTION1 up, ACTION2 down, ACTION3 left, ACTION4 right over the five-pixel grid. L2 route: reach the rhsxkxzdjz rotation trigger, re-enter it until rotation index 3, collect the lower and upper npxgalaybz step resets, then enter the target.

re86.registry_action_model: Keyboard ACTION1 up, ACTION2 down, ACTION3 left, ACTION4 right, ACTION5 cycles the active overlay source. L2 tail moves the active source downward and left, cycles, positions the next source upward/left, cycles again, then moves the final source down/left to cover the L2 target pixels. L3+: the single black pixel embedded in the active piece is the selection cursor; ACTION5 cycles which piece is selected, ACTION1-4 move it in exactly 3-pixel steps (targets must land on the piece anchor's mod-3 lattice). No coordinate clicks in this game.

sb26.registry_action_model: ACTION6 item click then ACTION6 slot click; ACTION5 validates. L2 tail uses display-center clicks derived from the offline environment source: (32,59)->(23,23), (18,59)->(29,23), (11,59)->(23,37), (46,59)->(29,37), (25,59)->(35,37), (53,59)->(41,37), (39,59)->(41,23), then validate. L3+: placed items are re-selectable -- clicking a placed item then an OCCUPIED slot swaps the two items (no reset needed to fix mistakes); a wrong ACTION5 validation is penalty-free.

sc25.registry_action_model: ACTION6 toggles cast cells at (24+5c,49+5r) or raw spell-select clicks; ACTION1-4 are tank-control moves with facing load-bearing. Exp4468 banked L2-L5 cumulative replay plans.

sk48.registry_action_model: Keyboard ACTION1-4 movement over the active chain head/selector; labels are compact JSON action rows emitted by the SK48 GameAdapter.

tn36.registry_action_model: ACTION6 click; data schema IS {x,y} and display->grid is 1:1 (camera.display_to_grid(30,13)==(30,13)). Clicks register (121/121 change the grid). Control is a PROGRAM/transform EDITOR, not direct steering: dispatch (tn36.py:2500) routes a click to a tool-palette (miytdaqzei, EMPTY at reset) else mvqheosngn(apply/2nd-object) else bzirenxmrg(the object); the object carries a move-program vkuvtkaerv=[3,0,3,0,0]; clicking it runs mmmdksslmq()->olrpupaury(). The exact EDIT->EXECUTE semantics that drive obj.y 13->33 are not yet cracked (directly invoking mmmdksslmq did NOT move the object; palette empty).

tr87.registry_action_model: keyboard [ACTION1-4]: ACTION1/2 cycle the SELECTED element's value (-1/+1 mod 7), ACTION3/4 move the selector. In base levels the selector picks an editable GLYPH; under alter_rules (L5-L6) it picks a rule SIDE (LHS or RHS; all glyphs in a side cycle together, preserving internal offsets). Move budget 128. L1: 14 actions/94 states. L2: +25 (39 tot)/152. L3: +21 (60 tot)/234. L4: +21 (81 tot)/319. L5: +14 (95 tot)/377. L6: +32 (127 tot)/511 (verifier-routed).

wa30.registry_action_model: ACTION1-5 keyboard only across all 9 levels. The banked 670-action route contains ZERO ACTION6 clicks, so any_oob_action6_clicks=False and it carries none of the live out-of-bounds risk that broke lf52's original L9 route. Solved by a 16-round OUTER-LOOP agent probe campaign (gpt-5.6-sol v1-v8 stalled at L1; claude-fable-5 v9-v16 broke through), NOT by an adapter and NOT by the live agent -- solve_provenance outer_loop_re, so it is never headline-eligible as live-agent capability.
